A LETTER TO OUR SHAREHOLDERS
Dear Fellow Shareholders -
2021 was an extraordinary year. The world, our country, our company, our people
and our patients continued to navigate the ongoing challenges of COVID-19 as we
all tried to return to some semblance of normalcy. Our clinicians remained on the
frontlines battling the Coronavirus and taking the best care of our nation’s most
frail populations amid a constantly challenging environment. Their unwavering
commitment to their patients is the hallmark of what we stand for here at Amedisys,
and that is a mission we hope you’re as proud of as we are. With that, let’s look back
PAUL KUSSEROW
at all we accomplished in 2021.
CHAIRMAN
OF THE BOARD
Though the pandemic pressed on, and the Delta variant swept the country, that
did not prevent us from seeing more than 445,000 patients while expanding our
footprint to 528 care centers spanning 38 states and the District of Columbia.
We generated adjusted revenue of $2.2B and adjusted EBITDA of $299.6M*, a 7%
and 10% increase over 2020, respectively. Our strategy of delivering true clinical
distinction, being an employer of choice, delivering operational excellence and
driving growth is simple yet very complex. These four pillars have been the
foundation of our organization and have helped drive the progress we have made
both this year and in years past. More specifically, here’s how we’ve progressed on
our four strategic pillars along with other key 2021 initiatives:
ACHIEVING CLINICAL DISTINCTION
One of the greatest achievements at Amedisys has been the rise to the best-in-class
quality in Home Health. When CMS began reporting on quality measures in 2015,
our Quality of Patient Care (QPC) rating was above the industry average at 3.49
Stars. Knowing that we are in the business of caring for people during vulnerable
times, we made a commitment to put patient quality at the heart of everything
we do. The tireless focus on quality since that point has propelled us to new
levels. Though CMS had frozen the publicly reported Home Health Stars metrics
during the pandemic, we never wavered from our focus on quality, and we are
proud to report that as of the January 2022 Quality of Patient Care Star score release,
our Home Health care centers averaged 4.33 Stars with 95% at 4 Stars

CMS had frozen the publicly reported Home Health Stars metrics
during the pandemic, we never wavered from our focus on quality, and we are
proud to report that as of the January 2022 Quality of Patient Care Star score release,
our Home Health care centers averaged 4.33 Stars with 95% at 4 Stars or above.
CHRIS GERARD Additionally, we have 37 care centers at 5 Stars. We are proud of our progress, but we
PRESIDENT AND CHIEF
will not rest as there is more work to be done in our commitment to continuing to
EXECUTIVE OFFICER
improve and lead in quality.
In our Hospice business, we continue to outperform the industry in all of the
Hospice Item Set (HIS) measures and are excited by the implementation of the new
Hospice Care Index which will give patients, families, referral sources and our
shareholders a view of how Amedisys Hospice quality compares to the rest of the
industry. We are equally committed to quality in Hospice as we are in Home Health,
and we commit that we will make progress towards being the industry’s leading
Hospice provider in quality.
Quality is a non-negotiable for us here at Amedisys, and we will never stop trying to
outperform ourselves. It is absolutely the right thing to do for our patients.

BECOMING AN EMPLOYER OF CHOICE
The labor environment today is unlike it has ever been in the past. The “Great Resignation,”
fueled by the constant pressures of the pandemic, have accelerated nurses retiring, leaving
practice or pushing many to travel or temporary work. Our clinicians are our most precious
asset as they drive our business by initiating and providing care, which drives revenues, while
the way in which they provide care drives quality. Today’s environment has forced us to
innovate around how we recruit our clinical staff and increased the importance of retaining
our clinicians. To help differentiate the way we recruit and to allow us to engage with
clinicians that want “gig” based work, we invested in ConnectRN. ConnectRN is an innovative
digital nurse staffing platform that offers shift-based work to clinicians. As we continue to
build the partnership, this platform will allow us to engage with clinicians differently and
offer them an additional level of flexibility. Look for more exciting progress

that want “gig” based work, we invested in ConnectRN. ConnectRN is an innovative
digital nurse staffing platform that offers shift-based work to clinicians. As we continue to
build the partnership, this platform will allow us to engage with clinicians differently and
offer them an additional level of flexibility. Look for more exciting progress in 2022 from our
ConnectRN partnership.
At Amedisys, we have taken a scientific approach to turnover by developing a turnover
prediction algorithm. This model allows us to identify employees with the highest risk of
leaving so we can then take action and intervene. In a time when most industries have seen
spikes in turnover, we ended 2021 with an overall voluntary turnover of 21.5%. We are proud
of that number but know we can and will do better. Ensuring we have the appropriate number
of clinicians to take on the increasing demand for our services is and will continue to be a
major initiative for the company.
OPERATIONAL EFFICIENCY
Performance in 2021 was undoubtedly impacted by the continuing effects of COVID-19. We
saw spikes in clinicians and associates on quarantine, changes in our referral patterns, patients
delaying care, elective procedures decline, return and decline again and through it all, we
still expanded our adjusted EBITDA margin by 40 basis points ending 2021 with a 13.6%
margin while delivering $189 million in cash flow from operations. For the full year 2021,
we performed 13.9 visits per episode, down 1 visit from 2020 and 3.1 visits from 2019 while
maintaining our quality scores. On clinical mix, we achieved 49.0% LPN utilization and 52.9%
PTA utilization. We are extremely proud of our organization’s performance during 2021 and
though we continue to feel the impacts of COVID-19 in 2022, we are once again confident that
we will deliver strong performance for our shareholders.
DRIVING GROWTH
Consistently growing all our lines of business will always be a key initiative
at Amedisys as our quality, strategy, scale and differentiated product
offering will drive outsized growth under normal market conditions.
However, growth in 2021 was significantly impacted by COVID-19 for all
the reasons we have previously discussed. That said, we were still able to
deliver total admissions growth in Home Health of 6% and total admission
growth in Hospice of 2%. These growth numbers

differentiated product
offering will drive outsized growth under normal market conditions.
However, growth in 2021 was significantly impacted by COVID-19 for all
the reasons we have previously discussed. That said, we were still able to
deliver total admissions growth in Home Health of 6% and total admission
growth in Hospice of 2%. These growth numbers were hard fought and hard
earned, but we know that we can do better, and we will.
From an inorganic growth perspective, we successfully signed and closed
nearly $300 million worth of deals including expanding our service offering
to higher acuity care via the Contessa Health acquisition. Our ability to
acquire and integrate has been a true competitive differentiator and will be
a big piece of our future growth story as we look to deploy capital to grow
both Home Health and Hospice in 2022.

INNOVATIONS
At Amedisys, we have a vision of caring for all patients in their homes regardless
of their acuity, payor type or care needs. Growing the number of patients we care
for and expanding the types of care we provide them has long been our desire. In
2021, we took a material step toward this goal when we acquired Contessa Health.
Contessa is a one-of-a-kind, tech-enabled, risk-taking care platform that provides
Hospital-at-Home and Skilled Nursing Facility (SNF) at Home services via joint
venture relationships with some of the most prestigious health systems and payors
in the U.S. The combined capabilities of Contessa and Amedisys create a truly
differentiated in-home care platform and allow for Amedisys to take risk for the care
of patients in their homes. We are extremely excited by the growth opportunities
of Contessa and even more excited by the increasing demand for the full suite of
in-home services that Amedisys now offers. Look for us to continue to iterate on the
Contessa model and grow the types of care we provide on the Contessa platform.
ENVIRONMENTAL, SOCIAL, GOVERNANCE (ESG)
The very nature of what we do and who we are at Amedisys allows us to have a voice
locally and nationally, and we strive to engage further in social issues impacting our
communities, patients, caregivers and associates. The full details of our ESG progress
and where we are heading on our ESG journey will be discussed in our

do and who we are at Amedisys allows us to have a voice
locally and nationally, and we strive to engage further in social issues impacting our
communities, patients, caregivers and associates. The full details of our ESG progress
and where we are heading on our ESG journey will be discussed in our first annual
ESG Report which will be published in June 2022. We understand that we must care
for the environment similarly to how we care for patients. Diversity and Inclusion
have been core tenants within our company culture as we recognize that different
opinions, views, experiences, upbringings and backgrounds help to drive innovative
thinking and bring well-rounded decision making. We have started a Diversity and
Inclusion Council that has worked to engage our diverse workforce and helped to
drive collaboration and conversation as we are continually innovating differentiated
ways to care for our patients and employees. We view our progress here as a material
driver of our future success and we are committed to doing all we can to provide
equal opportunities throughout our organization while being a value-add member
of our communities and an advocate for fairness and change at Amedisys, in our
industry and nationwide.
FUTURE OUTLOOK
2020 and 2021 were years unlike any of us have ever seen and yet Amedisys
performed at the top of the industry throughout the pandemic-induced volatility.
Though business has been impacted, the short-, medium- and long-term tailwinds
for care in the home and Amedisys are stronger than ever. The aging demographics
in the U.S., led by the Baby Boomers, will drive unprecedented demand for our
services. Our continued leadership in quality places us at the forefront of the
opportunity and our service line expansion with Contessa truly differentiates
Amedisys. We are creating a platform that goes beyond siloed Home Health,
Hospice, Personal Care and High-Acuity Care, one that will allow us to care for any
patient that wants to receive care at home regardless of their condition or disease
over a much longer time period than a traditional episode of care. Combine our
organic growth opportunity with our cash flow generation, low leverage and track
record of successful acquisition and integration and the Amedisys of the future looks
excitingly different than the Amedisys of today.

As you can see, the tailwinds driving our space and our company forward create a

FAREWELL... AND HELLO
Paul Kusserow:
“This is my last shareholder letter as I am moving to the role of Chairman, I’d like
to just say how proud and honored I am to have led this organization for the past
seven and a half years. It’s been a life changing journey to serve our patients and
employees! I believe the best time to transition leadership is when an organization
is at its peak strength, hitting on all cylinders, executing hard and has a strategy
that we know is a winner. The team we have built is second to none and knows
how to move our strategy to completion. I am leaving you all in the very capable
hands of Chris Gerard who is one of the best operators I’ve ever seen. It is an exciting
time to be at Amedisys. This is the right space, we are the highest quality asset and
I truly believe that the company we have built will lead, innovate and change how
healthcare is delivered in future. I am beyond excited to continue to watch this story
play out.”
Chris Gerard:
“Paul has had a profound impact on Amedisys during the seven and a half years
he led the company. Though he leaves big shoes to fill, I am truly excited by the
opportunity to continue the incredible story that is Amedisys. Over my 30-year
career in Home Health and Hospice, I can honestly say that I have never been
around a team that is so mission oriented and so focused on enabling our caregivers
to provide the highest quality in home care. We have differentiated ourselves and
positioned our organization to drive significant value to our shareholders as
we maximize the opportunities within our current operations and realize new
opportunities to leverage our assets in innovative ways. It really is an exciting time
to

focused on enabling our caregivers
to provide the highest quality in home care. We have differentiated ourselves and
positioned our organization to drive significant value to our shareholders as
we maximize the opportunities within our current operations and realize new
opportunities to leverage our assets in innovative ways. It really is an exciting time
to be an employee or a shareholder of Amedisys.”
THANK YOU
I sincerely hope that you as fellow shareholders can be equally as proud of the work being
done at the company as we are. The past two years have forced us to adapt, innovate and
change how we operate and how we make sure both our patients and employees are cared
for. We have learned much through this unprecedented time and one of the biggest takeaways
has been that home is the place to be. There is so much good to come and with your support,
Amedisys will continue to transform and lead how care is delivered in the home. Thank you.
Paul Kusserow Chris Gerard
Chairman of the Board President and Chief Executive Officer
